visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A close-up shot focuses on the control panel of a motorized baby swing. A man's hand, decorated with a dark beaded bracelet, reaches in to press the interface buttons. Directly beneath the swing, a red Milwaukee M18 power tool battery is suspended by a metal hook and wired into the swing's power intake. (2) The camera pans to the right to reveal a red Milwaukee Packout modular toolbox stacked on the wooden floor. The man, wearing a tan long-sleeved shirt and a black baseball cap worn backwards, opens the heavy lid. He retrieves a blue can of Red Bull and sets a red insulated tumbler on the lid. (3) Sitting comfortably on the red toolbox, the man uses both hands to assemble a baby bottle. He carefully takes the nipple and cap out of the red tumbler to combine them. To his left, a baby is lying in the swing, dressed in a white and green patterned onesie. (4) The man leans over the baby swing and holds the fully assembled bottle for the infant to feed. The indoor setting features warm wooden floors and matching wooden wall panels. The man is wearing white Puma slide sandals and dark joggers as he performs the caregiving task.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This comedic short presents a 'blue-collar' approach to parenting, humorously contrasting rugged manual labor tools with delicate childcare. By using industrial brands like Milwaukee to power a baby swing and serve as a mobile feeding station, the video creates a relatable meme about a handyman dad's resourceful yet unconventional methods.
